analysis:
This PR adds a `darkbloom waitlist` command and a client-side waitlist gate in front of `sandbox setup` (TB-013) and `cluster`.

Token handling (A-008):
- FeatureWaitlist.swift:92-98 accepts only an https base, or plain http to loopback. It rejects a base with a query or fragment.
- The provider login token (AuthTokenStore.load, WaitlistCommand.swift:36) is sent as a Bearer header (FeatureWaitlist.swift:125-127). Cookies are disabled.
- The NoRedirects delegate (FeatureWaitlist.swift:223-227) refuses redirects, so the token cannot be forwarded to another host.
- Responses are capped at 64 KiB and each call has a 10 s deadline (lines 195-219). This bounds coordinator-driven availability issues.
- The join body is `{}` and sends no machine data.

Terminal output:
- Coordinator-supplied text (title, summary, start_command, refusal and error strings) passes through printable() (View:131). It replaces Cc/Cf control and format characters and newlines with U+FFFD.
- JSON output escapes the same characters (View:139-152). This mitigates terminal injection from responses. The coordinator is trusted in any case.

Gate semantics:
- FeatureWaitlistGate.require (Gate:41-75) proceeds only on approved or on a 404 ("no such waitlist"). Every other outcome stops with exit 1 before installing.
- The 404 fail-open is intentional, for coordinators released before waitlists existed.
- This gate is local UX and is trivially bypassable by an operator (ADV-001). It must not be treated as authorization. Backend enforcement of sandbox/cluster approval is platform-owned and not in this evidence.
- No threat-model control relied on it, so no regression was found.

SandboxSetupCommand:
- It adds `var waitlist: FeatureWaitlistAccess = .live()` (head ~164-166), which reads the default config path rather than any `--config` option.
- That is at most a functional mismatch about which coordinator is asked. The token still goes only to a configured https/loopback coordinator.
- The call site (head 277-295) was not in this batch's units. Integration should confirm the gate runs before the installer download and execution (TB-013/T-061), and that `--yes` maps to joinWithoutAsking only.

The ClusterWaitlistGateTests file is test-only and was reviewed via metadata and excerpt.

Threat-model note: TB-013 could mention the new account-scoped coordinator call made before setup, and the 404 fail-open behavior.
